newsitem.title: USA: Court orders extradition for Irish fugitives.
newsitem.headline: Court orders extradition for Irish fugitives.

text.p: A federal judge ruled on Monday that three fugitives from a Northern Ireland prison may be extradited to Britan.
U.S. District Judge Charles Legge rejected the arguments of Kevin Artt, Pol Brennan and Terence Kirby, that they would be harmed or killed if they were returned to British custody.

Artt, Brennan and Kirby were among 38 prisoners who escaped from Northern Ireland's Maze Prison in 1983. Artt was arrested in June 1992, in San Diego, and Brennan and Kirby were arrested in the San Francisco area in 1993 and 1994 respectively.

"This court certifies the extraditability of respondents Artt, Brennan and Kirby," Legge said in a written ruling. He also ordered the three men, who had been free on bail, to surrender to U.S. Marshalls immediately. who had been free on bail, to surrender to U.S. Marshalls immediately.
Legge said that the three men were each convicted of crimes of violence in Northern Ireland "based upon substantial evidence and with appropriate judicial procedures."
Legge said the three would not be punished or detained if they were returned to Northern Ireland because of their race, religion, nationality or political opinions.
